steps.text: The sensation is hard to describe.
There's a strange itch on her forehead. The halo atop her crown flickers with no rhyme or reason.
Her view begins, gradually, to dim.
Yes, Fortuna can see the wrinkled abbot's incredulous gaze, and hear the noise of the onlooking crowd.
But she attempts to feel the old man's mind, as she may have done every time before, and yet his emotions no longer drift their way into her soul, not even a hint or trace—
She cannot sense the other Sankta.
She is no longer one amongst them.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: Fallen...?

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: What's the meaning of this...? What's happening to Fortuna? Is—Is she sick?

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: I'll explain on the way back. First, we handle the pressing matters here—

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: Avus Stefano!

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: Save Fina! I'm begging you, save her, hurry!

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: Child, do not panic. Tell me clearly... what is it that happened?

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: Fina—Fina was bleeding everywhere, and I couldn't stop it... I couldn't find anyone to help...

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: It was—It was just a dumb fight—Fina wanted my patron firearm—I should have just given it to her—why didn't I give it to her?

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: It's all my fault...!

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: Fear not, fear not, child. There is naught to fear.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: As informed by present circumstances, I would consider this a case of accidental injury with no subjective intent to harm.

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: Silence! Executor!

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: You would accuse this child... of aggrieving her own kin?!

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: How can your finger know to lay such blame—?!

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: It is the most rational assumption.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Rejection by the Commandments is not insurmountable. Unintentional discharges are particularly common.

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: The sheer drivel!

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: No... he's right... it was me, I pulled the trigger!

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: Fortuna! No, you...

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: Avus Stefano, it was my fault! I'll take it however they punish me!

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: But Fina's still... She's been hurt! Please, you have to save her!

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: Fine, fine, I'll see to it now—

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: I'll go.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: I'm good with first aid. Give me a location.

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: Just—Just go to my room...

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: I can show you the way!

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: If you would, Clément.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: Less talk, more action. Move.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: This way! Follow me!

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: Here, right here!

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: The door's wide open...

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: Oh, the blood...

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: Delfina!

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: Quiet down! You want everyone to hear about this?!

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: Move, let me work!

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: No. She's in bad shape. Bleeding's too profuse.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: And her wound is...

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: What do we do now?

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: Flowers... right! I remember His Excellency saying the sacrarium's flowers could be used for healing! Yes, right, they have to be...

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: Wait while I pick some!

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: Don't bother.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: Let me go! If I—If I leave right now, we might still make it—

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: There's no point! Even if we stop the bleeding, we're out of time!

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: What? How can there be no point...?

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: Because there isn't one.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: She was shot point blank. Severe loss of blood. I can't detect breathing.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: I've tried first aid. Nothing. I couldn't get a pulse.

spans.text: first aid. Nothing. I couldn't get a pulse.

steps.name: Clément
steps.text: No breath... and no pulse...

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: It's very likely she was taken instantly.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: The girl is dead.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: I've locked the entrance. No one was around, fortunately. We can't have many eyewitnesses.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: How are we handling this?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: We wait for Serpilia to conclude treatment.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Halo discoloration is characteristic of a fallen angel. She is falling rapidly.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: With consideration for stability within the monastery, this is my suggestion: cancel the sermon and lock down all news of this.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I have a proposal.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: In order to avert unnecessary conflict, I and my colleagues will take over patrol duty for the following interim.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: All inhabitants should return to their rooms as soon as possible, and await final verdict tomorrow.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: This will ensure to the maximum extent that there are no further accidents.

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: Reverend Executor, this abbey is not under Lateran jurisdiction until it arrives at its final destination!

spans.text: under Lateran jurisdiction until it arrives at its final destination!

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I am aware.

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: We can address any problems within the monastery on our own. We wouldn't hassle our Lateran visitors.

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: As you so rightly indicated, Reverend Executor, this was simply an accident. Given we still don't know Delfina's condition, this could all be a false alarm...

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Accident or not, she has fallen.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: It is mandatory that issues of fallen angels are assessed and addressed personally by His Holiness and the Sacred College of Cardinals.

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: So you want to take her back to Laterano. Not that I've once seen a two-horned Sankta in Laterano, not ever!

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: Tell me, Reverend Executor, how can her being 'addressed' inspire trust in me?

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: Well... Federico, I'm just mentioning this, but didn't His Holiness tell you to keep an eye on how often you contradict people?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: What? I am not manifesting any contradiction.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: Err, okay. I mean... um, your approach could be a little more conciliatory...

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I do not understand your meaning.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: But thank you for the suggestion.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: You... *sigh* I'll take it.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: I think... we're not going to get anywhere arguing about it here. Seeing as we can't leave for now anyway, we might want to find a place for, um, Seniora Fortuna here to catch her breath for a while.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: Once we have the situation under control, and everyone's calmed down somewhat, we'll still have plenty of time to discuss how exactly we resolve this.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: And, Most Reverend Abbot, you don't have to be so wary of Laterano. Similar cases have happened before. As long as we're sure the Commandments weren't violated with malice, the punishment should be light, at most.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: Right, Federico?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Correct. But you did not have the authority to divulge that information, Richele.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: Look, special circumstances.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: Just, the both of you, consider it?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I have no objection.

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: I worry...

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: ...Avus Stefano, don't...

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: It was my fault... Whatever the punishment is, I'll accept it...

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: Fortuna!

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: I'll go with you, Senior...

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: Then we're decided.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: I'll find Seniora Fortuna somewhere to rest. You two stay here for the moment and calm down.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: This room looks good enough. Err... very spacious to boot.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: Don't worry too much. Your case is a relatively special one, and I imagine His Holiness will get personally involved. As long as there wasn't intent to harm, it shouldn't end up too severe.

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: Fina's...

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: Is Fina, um... the wounded Sankta citizen?

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: We still can't be sure of her condition, but my colleague should be treating her now. Let's think positive—things may not be that bad.

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: My horns...

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: Hm?

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: I wonder why I'm growing...

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: Horns like a Sarkaz's...?

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: Well, that, I'm not too sure myself... In any case, someone will tell you once we're in Laterano.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: For now, just rest up here.

steps.name: Fortuna
steps.text: ...Okay.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: I'll be outside the door. If you need anything, just knock for me.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: *sigh*... Who knows how Federico's going to handle this.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: You know what? I am a pretty sensitive guy, if I'm being honest. I always get this cold sweat when someone's creeping around behind me.

spans.text: a pretty sensitive guy, if I'm being honest. I always get this cold sweat when someone's creeping around behind me.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: The fun's over. Come out, Oren.

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: Just one question—how'd you see me?

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: I was just bluffing, actually. I didn't think you would come out.

spans.text: I was just bluffing, actually. I didn't think you

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: You're not expecting me to believe that, are you?

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: Why not? I'm good either way.

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: Whatever, Richele, you little cheat.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: Don't say that. I'm more honest than Serpilia, at least.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: She's one of yours, isn't she? She was lying.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: No... not outright, I guess. She just declined to say everything.

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: Where is this coming from?

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: We were asking her about her relation to you. All she effectively said was 'I couldn't care less about him' without revealing anything else.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: She was dodging Federico's questions.

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: And that's your entire reason for saying she was lying? Don't you think that's a weird conclusion?

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: I think having the same skill under my belt helps. Besides, look at the situation here. It's easy to guess how you'd act, and I'd also guess Federico's guessed.

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: There's no winning with you.

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: Plan A should've been dragging him off for drinks, after all.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: Followed by him carting you back to the Lateran?

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: This monastery's guests have more swagger than you think. Can't say Federico would care to wrangle me once it's all going down.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: Sounds like trouble really is brewing here.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: So, Oren, what are you and Serpilia planning exactly?

steps.name: Oren
steps.text: Once you hear me out, are you gonna help me?

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: Thaaat... remains to be seen.

steps.name: Richele
steps.text: I'd have to hear the answer first to decide.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: Federico, I've got bad news.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: Uh... wait, is there anyone with you?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Richele is not here.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: Who cares about him!

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: I mean... is that Fortuna kid with you?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: No. Richele escorted her to her accommodations.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: If you have discovered anything, please inform me. I require confirmation of the aggrieved citizen's condition.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: Fine. Then I'll give it to you straight—we were too late.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Confirmed deceased?

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: Confirmed. It was a fatal gunshot wound. Barring a true miracle, she's not coming back to life.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: Oh, and the guy with me called Clément. He said he was going to pick some flowers, and I didn't care. I let him go.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: He was out of his mind when he left...

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Flowers?

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: Per the intel. The abbey's specialty. Not many left right now, I gather, and that's not important.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: The whole was an accident, Federico. The girl wasn't lying. Accidental discharge. It might not... be all that severe...

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: His Holiness will judge.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: Sure... I mean, even Mostima flies with him. I'm sure Our Holiness will forgive with wide arms just like always.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: I'll contact Richele in a bit—I'm sure he misses being free range. It'll be me watching the girl. I won't let her run off.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: As for how Lemuen and Oren are doing...

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Has Oren Argiolas made contact with you?

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: Am I under suspicion here?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: By my judgment, yes.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Oren's movements were not placed under any restrictions. Failure to contact the Lateran is conduct of his own subjective.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: The Sarkaz are involved in these affairs. I conjecture Oren would not immediately leave. If he wanted all leeway for operation, it would require finding a collaborator.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: And so you suspect me... But what about Richele? No thoughts about him?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Richele does not have as ample time to act alone as you do. His level of suspicion ranks below yours.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: Hahaha. You're a smart cookie, Federico.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: Here's my comment: no comment. All guesses here are yours. I haven't said a thing.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: Good? Good. I'll be in touch.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: Oh, yeah, is the Abbot there?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Serpilia
steps.text: Uh... are you going to relay the news to him?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: That is unnecessary.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: He has heard it.

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: ...Delfina...

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: I must see for myself. I need to... see the child...

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Your Excellency may act freely.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: However, Serpilia would not misjudge. I do not recommend spending additional time on reconfirming.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I am tentatively assuming Oren Argiolas is still aboard, and has some sort of scheme.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I must now ascertain in detail all movements he made prior to his disappearance staying at this monastery, as well as all recent absences and returns of monastery personnel. I ask you comply.

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: Reverend Executor, what is necessity to you? What line do you draw between the necessary and unnecessary?

spans.text: necessity to you? What line do you draw between the necessary and unnecessary?

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: Can you truly not hear your kin lamenting? Does emotion truly mean nothing in your mind?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: I will not deny that.

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: And should that be, you are no worthy harbinger of Paradise.

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: And should you represent Laterano...

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: Laterano is no worthy shepherd of my faith.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Please answer my questions, Your Excellency: Has Oren acted abnormally in any way within the monastery? Have any other people lodged recently at the monastery?

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: My words are wasted on you.

steps.name: Abbot
steps.text: Do as you will, Reverend Executor.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Finished...

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Trust him to use up every last page of a notebook this thick.
Lemuen heaves a sigh, and closes the antique plain colored notebook shut.
Her fingers trace over the nicks and scrapes that decorate the cover, each one hiding a story of its own.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: If back then...

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Oh, what am I thinking?

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Right, now then... Hm, it's time I got to work myself.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: With Serpilia's group already here, I can't keep on dawdling.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Hm?

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Is someone outside? If you're looking for me, you can come right in.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Well, well, that's not a guest I'd expect.

steps.name: Lemuen
steps.text: Sorry, visitor, but you came at a bad time—I don't have any tea to offer you.
